name: Shulammite
title: The Beloved in the Song of Solomon
summary: The Shulammite is the female protagonist in Solomon's Song of Songs, a beautiful young woman who is the object of the king's love and desire. She represents the ideal bride and has been interpreted both literally as Solomon's beloved and allegorically as a picture of the relationship between God and his people, or between Christ and the church.

keyEvents.title: The Shulammite's Longing for Her Beloved
keyEvents.description: The Shulammite expresses her deep longing and love for her beloved and asks him to kiss her. She describes his love as better than wine.

keyEvents.title: The Shulammite Describes Herself
keyEvents.description: The Shulammite describes herself as dark but beautiful, sunburnt from working in the vineyards. She explains that her brothers put her in charge of watching over the vineyards.

keyEvents.title: Mutual Declaration of Love
keyEvents.description: The Shulammite and her beloved exchange declarations of love and praise each other's beauty. They rejoice in one another in a garden full of flowers and fragrance.

keyEvents.title: The Shulammite Seeks Her Beloved at Night
keyEvents.description: The Shulammite tells how she sought her beloved in the city streets at night and finally found him. She holds on to him and will not let him go.

keyEvents.title: The Beauty of the Shulammite Is Praised
keyEvents.description: The beloved gives a detailed description of the Shulammite's beauty from head to toe and declares that she is perfect and without flaw.

keyEvents.title: The Shulammite's Declaration of Faithfulness
keyEvents.description: The Shulammite declares that love is as strong as death, and that many waters cannot quench love. This is the climax of the Song of Songs and a profound theological statement about the power of love.
